digest.headline: US stock futures and Wall Street slide as Democrats make midterm gains.

lede.b: US stock futures and Wall Street fell because Democrats made gains in the midterm elections, which means voters changed who controls the US legislature. Nasdaq futures dropped 2%. When stock futures fall, it means investors expect share prices to go down when the market opens. Treasury yields, which are the interest payments the government pays on its loans, fell following the congressional outcome. Gold prices climbed as a softer dollar boosted bullion demand.
lede.i: US stock futures and Wall Street slid as investors digested a political shake-up following Democratic midterm election gains. Nasdaq futures dropped 2% on the surprise congressional outcome. Treasury yields fell alongside the dollar following the sweep, which drove gold prices higher as bullion demand increased. Wall Street registered losses as market participants weighed the legislative shift.
lede.a: US stock futures and Wall Street slid after Democrats captured Congress in the midterm elections. Nasdaq futures dropped 2% on the congressional outcome, while Treasury yields and the dollar fell in tandem. Gold climbed on the back of the softer greenback, and Wall Street registered broader losses as investors priced in the legislative shift.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US markets react to Democratic midterm election gains

stories.t: US stock futures and Wall Street slide after midterm elections
stories.b: Stock futures are contracts to buy or sell shares at a future date, and their prices show what people expect the market to do. Wall Street fell because Democrats made gains in the midterm elections in Washington. Nasdaq futures slid by 2.0%.
stories.i: US stock futures fell as investors digested a political shake-up in Washington. Wall Street declined as Democrats made midterm gains. Nasdaq futures dropped 2% following the surprise congressional outcome.
stories.a: Wall Street equities retreated as market participants priced in the implications of a Democratic congressional sweep. Nasdaq futures slid 2.0% amid a broader reassessment of Washington policy risks. Equity indices registered sharp declines as the midterm results disrupted consensus expectations.

stories.t: Treasury yields and the dollar fall while gold climbs
stories.b: Treasury yields, which are like the interest paid on government loans, fell after Democrats swept Congress. Gold climbed higher because the US dollar became softer. Wall Street fell as Democrats made midterm gains.
stories.i: Treasury yields fell following a Democratic sweep of Congress. Gold climbed as a softer dollar boosted bullion demand. Wall Street registered losses as investors weighed the legislative shift.
stories.a: Sovereign debt yields dropped across the curve as a Democratic sweep in Congress reshaped fiscal expectations. Spot gold extended gains as the US dollar softened in response to the political outcome. Market pricing adjusted rapidly to the altered legislative outlook.

politics.b: Democrats made gains in the midterm elections in Washington and swept Congress. Investors reacted to this political shake-up by selling stocks.
politics.i: Democrats secured a sweep of Congress in the midterm elections. Markets adjusted asset prices to reflect the new legislative alignment in Washington.
politics.a: The midterm elections produced a Democratic sweep of Congress. Capital markets immediately priced in the policy and fiscal consequences of the altered legislative majority.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Bank of England rate decision and pound at seven-week high

stories.b: The Bank of England is the group that sets the main interest rate for the country. Analysts expect this group to raise the cost of borrowing soon. Mortgage rates hit a three-year high as people waited for this decision. The pound reached a seven-week high against other currencies.
stories.i: The Bank of England approaches a crunch vote on its key rate. Mortgage rates climbed to a three-year high ahead of the decision. Meanwhile, the pound traded at a seven-week high against a weakening dollar.
stories.a: The Bank of England faces expectations to join international peers in tightening monetary policy. UK mortgage pricing scaled three-year highs as markets priced in the looming rate action. Sterling touched a seven-week high supported by dollar weakness.

stories.b: The FTSE 100 is an index, which is a basket of shares representing the largest companies listed on the London stock market. This index opened 0.04% higher and ticked up further. Falling bond yields, which are returns paid on government debt, helped miners offset losses in the defence sector.
stories.i: The FTSE 100 index opened 0.04% higher and ticked up in cautious trading ahead of the central bank outcome. Falling gilt yields supported equities. Mining stocks offset losses in the defence sector.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 opened 0.04% higher as investors traded defensively ahead of the Monetary Policy Committee outcome. Declining sovereign debt yields cushioned broader equities. Mining sector gains offset losses in defence issues.

politics.b: Politicians discussed housing costs as mortgage rates climbed to a three-year high.
politics.i: Political focus turned to household finances as mortgage rates reached a three-year high ahead of the Bank of England decision.
politics.a: Policy debate centered on housing affordability metrics as mortgage products touched three-year highs prior to the central bank meeting.

timeline: FTSE 100 opens 0.04% higher ahead of Bank of England rate decision

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German stocks rise and wages rise

stories.b: The DAX index is a basket that tracks the forty biggest companies in Germany, like a shopping list of the nation's top corporate giants. This DAX index opened 0.44% higher. Later, the DAX index traded above 26,000 points after a 0.9% daily gain. Frankfurt stocks opened higher as investors digested elections in the United States.
stories.i: The DAX index opened 0.44% higher in Frankfurt. European shares rose as a Democratic sweep lifted clean energy and bank stocks. The DAX index later traded above 26,000 following a 0.9% daily gain.
stories.a: The DAX index opened 0.44% higher, tracking broader European share momentum following a Democratic sweep that buoyed clean energy and bank equities. The index subsequently breached 26,000 points after recording a 0.9% daily gain.

stories.t: European Central Bank Tracker Shows Higher Wage Growth
stories.b: The European Central Bank is the big bank that sets money rules for countries using the euro. This European Central Bank released a wage tracker. The European Central Bank wage tracker suggests slightly higher wage growth in the first three quarters of 2027 compared with the full year of 2026.
stories.i: The European Central Bank published data on compensation trends. The European Central Bank wage tracker suggests slightly higher wage growth in the first three quarters of 2027 compared with the full year of 2026.
stories.a: The European Central Bank released compensation metrics via its proprietary monitor. The inflation backdrop frames the European Central Bank wage tracker data, which suggests slightly higher wage growth in the first three quarters of 2027 compared with the full year of 2026.

politics.b: Investors in Germany watched political events in the United States, including midterm elections.
politics.i: Market participants in Germany digested the results and political uncertainty stemming from the United States midterm elections.
politics.a: Equities in Frankfurt absorbed cross-border inflation and political uncertainty following the United States midterm elections.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Tokyo shares fall and yen climbs amid market developments

stories.b: Tokyo shares tumble on Wednesday despite strong corporate earnings. Tokyo equities drop as the Nikkei 225 falls. Japan futures fall for the fourth consecutive session. Asian shares and United States futures show mixed trading.
stories.i: Tokyo shares decline on Wednesday despite corporate earnings releases. The Nikkei 225 drops alongside a fall in Tokyo equities. Japan futures extend their losses to a fourth consecutive session.
stories.a: Tokyo equities retreat on Wednesday despite corporate earnings reports. The Nikkei 225 index contracts as regional sentiment deteriorates. Japan futures record a fourth consecutive session of declines.

stories.t: Japanese Yen Rises and Officials Monitor Moves
stories.b: The Japanese currency jumps and trims earlier gains as the United States dollar recovers. Traders worry about potential currency market intervention by authorities. Japanese official Kihara states that officials will watch market moves with a high sense of urgency.
stories.i: The Japanese yen climbs amid intervention fears and a softer United States dollar. The currency later trims some gains as the dollar recovers from post-election reversals. Official Kihara declares that authorities will watch market moves with a high sense of urgency.
stories.a: The Japanese yen appreciates on intervention fears and dollar weakness before trimming gains during United States dollar recovery. Ministry official Kihara commits to monitoring market movements with a high sense of urgency.

politics.a: Mitsui & Co outlines fiscal year 2028 targets aiming for net income surpassing 1.1 trillion yen and an ROE exceeding 12% through growth investments. Separately, authorities arrest a South Korean citizen over the export of automobiles valued at 220 million yen to Russia.
politics.c: Mitsui & Co CEO targets a net profit exceeding 1.1 trillion yen and an ROE above 12% by fiscal year 2028, driven by growth investments. Meanwhile, law enforcement arrests a South Korean national for exporting cars valued at 220 million yen to Russia.

China.label: China
China.sub: China defends yuan and banks join stock loan scheme

stories.t: PBOC defends yuan and raises reserve requirements
stories.b: The People's Bank of China manages the country's money and recently nudged its official reference rate higher. It also raised the foreign exchange reserve requirement ratio. This rule forces financial institutions to hold more foreign currency. The central bank took these steps to curb a rally in the yuan.
stories.i: The PBOC nudged its reference rate higher and increased the foreign exchange reserve requirement ratio. These twin actions aim to curb the recent rally in the yuan. European policymakers are simultaneously targeting the exchange rate to counter low-cost Chinese export advantages.
stories.a: The PBOC adjusted its daily reference rate and raised reserve requirements on foreign exchange holdings to temper the yuan. Such measures directly respond to external pressure from Europe regarding low-cost export pricing advantages. This intervention occurs while domestic demand pressures and weak property starts persist.

stories.t: Chinese lenders apply over 200 billion yuan for stock loans
stories.b: Chinese banks applied for more than 200 billion yuan through a special central bank stock loan scheme. At the same time, the national team engaged in buying assets to defend local markets. Cinda Real Estate reported a net loss of 1.2 billion yuan for the third quarter. This loss came as property sector challenges continued.
stories.i: Chinese banks submitted applications exceeding 200 billion yuan for a PBOC stock loan facility. State-backed entities simultaneously engaged in national team buying and share buybacks to defend equity valuations. Cinda Real Estate posted a third-quarter net loss of 1.2 billion yuan amid ongoing property sector distress.
stories.a: Commercial lenders applied for over 200 billion yuan via the PBOC stock loan mechanism to support equity markets. Authorities deployed national team purchases and buybacks as property starts plunged to 2002 levels. Cinda Real Estate reflected these sectoral headwinds by posting a 1.2 billion yuan third-quarter net loss.

politics.b: Chinese authorities intervened in financial markets with stock loans and reserve adjustments. Europe pressured the yuan exchange rate amid low-cost export challenges. The property sector suffered deep declines as state firms posted heavy losses.
politics.i: Chinese authorities defended domestic equity and foreign exchange markets through the PBOC and national team interventions. European scrutiny targeted the yuan as property starts plummeted to 2002 levels. State enterprises faced dual pressures from domestic demand contraction and external trade frictions.
politics.a: Policymakers combined reserve requirement hikes with equity purchase defenses to stabilize domestic markets against persistent property sector deleveraging. European trade focus on the yuan compounded export pressures alongside weak domestic demand. Real estate distress deepened as state-backed developers recorded major quarterly losses.

timeline: China raised the foreign exchange reserve requirement ratio to curb the yuan rally.
Cinda Real Estate reported a third-quarter net loss of 1.2 billion yuan.
Bank applications for the PBOC stock loan scheme exceeded 200 billion yuan.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI liquidity operations, T-bill auctions and equity moves

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Conducts Treasury Bill Auctions
stories.b: The central bank of a country manages money and interest rates. It held an auction for short-term government debt called T-bills, which are like IOUs that pay back money after a set period. The Reserve Bank of India sold 91-day T-bills worth 8,000 crore rupees and 364-day T-bills worth 7,000 crore rupees. Investors received yields, which are the overall returns on their investment, of 5.8970% for the shorter bills and 6.6485% for the longer ones. No 182-day T-bills were accepted in this round.
stories.i: The central bank issued short-term sovereign debt across multiple maturities to manage cash levels. The 91-day gilts brought a yield to maturity of 5.8970% on an accepted face value of 8,000 crore rupees. Meanwhile, the 364-day paper cleared at a yield of 6.6485% for 7,000 crore rupees of accepted bids. The intermediate 182-day auction received no accepted allocations.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed liquidity through primary issuance across the 91-day and 364-day buckets while leaving the 182-day tranche completely unallocated. The 91-day paper printed a cut-off price of 98.5511 with a 5.8970% yield, whereas the 364-day issuance cleared at 93.7820 yielding 6.6485%. Total notified amounts reached 8,000 crore rupees for both the shortest and middle tenors alongside 7,000 crore rupees for the longest tenor.

stories.t: Central Bank Executes Overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo Auctions
stories.b: A central bank sometimes borrows cash from commercial banks to reduce the amount of money moving around the economy. The Reserve Bank of India ran two overnight variable rate reverse repo auctions on November 4, 2026. For the first auction, banks offered 73,907 crore rupees, and the bank accepted 50,015 crore rupees at a cut-off rate of 5.49%. For the second auction, banks offered 1,180 crore rupees, and the central bank accepted all of it at the same rate of 5.49%.
stories.i: The central bank conducted daily liquidity management using overnight variable rate reverse repo windows to drain surplus cash. The first operation drew 73,907 crore rupees in total offers against a notified amount of 50,000 crore rupees, with 50,015 crore rupees accepted at 5.49%. A subsequent second round accepted the entirety of the 1,180 crore rupees offered by lenders at the matching 5.49% rate.
stories.a: Open market liquidity management saw the Reserve Bank of India execute primary and secondary overnight variable rate reverse repo absorptions. The initial 50,000 crore rupee notified window attracted 73,907 crore rupees in bids, forcing a partial acceptance rate of 67.64% at a 5.49% cut-off. The supplementary reverse repo absorbed an additional 1,180 crore rupees at the identical weighted average rate of 5.49%.

politics.b: The Reserve Bank of India set up a new technical committee for financial markets on November 4, 2026. Stock indexes such as the Sensex rose by 118 points, while the Nifty index stayed near 23,900. Information technology stocks dropped in value, but defence and consumer goods companies saw their share prices climb. Foreign financial inflows remained weak, keeping pressure on the Indian rupee.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India constituted the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets on November 4, 2026, to engage with market participants. Equity benchmarks climbed as the Sensex advanced 118 points and the Nifty held near the 23,900 level. Sectoral performance diverged as IT equities declined while defence and consumer names rallied amid subdued foreign capital inflows.
politics.a: The Reserve Bank of India formalized the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets on November 4, 2026, responding to structural market evolution. Equity gauges advanced moderately with the Sensex gaining 118 points and the Nifty hovering near 23,900, underpinned by strength in defence and consumer counters despite broad IT sector weakness. Persistent sluggishness in foreign inflows continued to weigh on the rupee.

timeline: Money market operations recorded total overnight volumes of 7,55,006.14 crore rupees.
The Reserve Bank of India constituted the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets.
The central bank executed T-bill auctions and variable rate reverse repo operations.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Brazilian stocks fall ahead of Copom decision

stories.t: Petrobras and Vale Slide as Stocks Fall Ahead of Decision
stories.b: Brazilian stocks fell before an upcoming decision by Copom, which is the committee that decides interest rates. Companies like Petrobras and Vale saw their share prices drop. Petrobras also faced share sales by ARGA Investment Management LP and prepared to release its earnings. Meanwhile, bp and Petrobras found hydrocarbons in separate deepwater wells offshore Brazil.
stories.i: Brazilian stocks dropped as markets positioned themselves ahead of the Copom rate decision. Petrobras and Vale shares slid, dragging down the Bovespa index to 165,569.36 points. ARGA Investment Management LP sold 209,140 shares of Petrobras ahead of its earnings release. Separately, bp and Petrobras discovered hydrocarbons in offshore deepwater wells.
stories.a: The Bovespa closed down at 165,569.36 points driven by declines in Petrobras and Vale ahead of the Copom meeting. ARGA Investment Management LP divested 209,140 shares of Petrobras prior to the company's earnings announcement. Concurrently, upstream developments confirmed hydrocarbon finds by bp and Petrobras in separate deepwater wells offshore.

politics.a: The sources contain no political data or official government announcements for Brazil.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco Q3 earnings, output, and budget deficit updates

stories.t: Aramco Posts Q3 Income and Pipeline Growth
stories.src: Azərtac · صحيفة مال · ASHARQ AL-AWSAT English
stories.b: Saudi Aramco raised its adjusted net income by 9% in the third quarter. The company also advanced its East-West Pipeline expansion. The CFO stated that the firm does not need to borrow money to cover shortfalls. Brand Finance valued Aramco as the world's second most valuable oil and gas brand at $47.3bn.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco reported a 9% increase in adjusted net income for the third quarter. The company advanced its East-West Pipeline expansion project. The CFO confirmed that the firm holds no need to borrow to cover funding shortfalls. Brand Finance valued the firm as the world's second most valuable oil and gas brand at $47.3bn.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco posted a 9% rise in adjusted net income for the third quarter alongside the ongoing advancement of the East-West Pipeline expansion. The CFO reiterated that the balance sheet requires no external borrowing to service funding shortfalls. Brand Finance assessed the firm as the world's second most valuable oil and gas brand at $47.3bn.

stories.t: OPEC Production and Budget Deficit Pressures
stories.b: OPEC and its allies kept output steady while Gulf shipping remained under threat. Crude oil prices rose on supply concerns despite OPEC making its sixth demand forecast cut. Meanwhile, the Saudi budget deficit more than doubled due to war and Aramco fees. Aramco also started production from a giant oilfield expansion project.
stories.i: OPEC and its allies kept oil output steady while Gulf shipping remained under threat. Crude oil prices climbed on supply concerns despite OPEC issuing its sixth demand forecast cut. The Saudi budget deficit more than doubled due to war and Aramco fees. Aramco separately started production from a giant oilfield expansion project.
stories.a: OPEC and its allies maintained steady output quotas while Gulf shipping routes remained under threat. Crude oil spot prices advanced on supply worries despite OPEC delivering its sixth consecutive demand forecast cut. The sovereign budget deficit more than doubled, driven by war expenses and Aramco fees, while Aramco brought a giant oilfield expansion project on stream.

politics.b: Saudi Arabia faces a budget deficit that more than doubled due to war. Gulf shipping remains under threat from regional conflict. OPEC and its allies keep oil output steady.
politics.i: The Saudi budget deficit more than doubled due to war and Aramco fees. Gulf shipping routes remain under threat amid regional conflict. OPEC and its allies decided to keep oil output steady.
politics.a: The sovereign fiscal deficit more than doubled, burdened by war expenditures and Aramco fees. Gulf shipping infrastructure remains under persistent threat from ongoing conflict. OPEC and its allies maintained steady output targets.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira exchange rates, corporate earnings and reserves

stories.b: Nigeria has its own money called the naira. Businesses use foreign money like the US dollar to trade across borders. Airtel Africa made four hundred and fifty-two million dollars in profit. That is an increase of 20.5%. The company earned 28% more money because the naira recovered.
stories.i: Airtel Africa reported a profit increase of 20.5% to $452m. A stronger naira lifted company revenue by 28%. Meanwhile, the official exchange rate reached ₦1,346.43 per dollar. The parallel market traded at ₦1,390.
stories.a: Airtel Africa posted a 20.5% profit rise to $452m as a 28% revenue expansion followed naira appreciation. Official NAFEX quotes positioned the currency at ₦1,346.43 per dollar, while unofficial channels priced transactions at ₦1,390.

stories.src: Business Post Nigeria · Legit News · The Guardian Nigeria News
stories.b: The naira gained 0.07% against the US dollar at the official NAFEX window. Nigeria keeps a pool of money from other countries called foreign reserves. These reserves recorded their slowest monthly growth of the year 2026. Commercial banks released new dollar pricing lists as the currency traded high.
stories.i: The naira appreciated by 0.07% against the US dollar at the NAFEX window. Nigeria recorded its slowest monthly growth in foreign reserves for 2026. Commercial banks including Access, UBA, and Zenith published updated dollar rates.
stories.a: The naira recorded a 0.07% gain against the US dollar at the NAFEX trading window. Foreign reserves registered their slowest monthly expansion trajectory of 2026. Deposit money institutions including Access, UBA, and Zenith issued revised foreign exchange pricing schedules.

politics.b: President Tinubu implemented economic reforms. The World Bank reported on these changes in Nigeria. Political shifts in the United States caused the US dollar to weaken.
politics.i: The World Bank published an assessment detailing President Tinubu's economic reforms. Concurrently, US political developments involving Democrats taking control exerted downward pressure on the US dollar.
politics.a: The World Bank released an evaluation focusing on President Tinubu's structural reforms. Democratic ascendance in the United States triggered dollar weakness, altering external valuation dynamics for emerging markets.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Australian Dollar reacts to RBA interest rate decision

stories.t: Reserve Bank of Australia delivers interest rate hike
stories.b: The central bank of Australia, which manages the country's money and interest rates, raised its rate. Currency markets reacted immediately to the decision. Commerzbank analysts noted that financial markets doubt the central bank will raise rates further. The Australian Dollar moved following the announcement.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of Australia implemented an interest rate hike. Foreign exchange markets reacted to the policy shift. Commerzbank noted that market participants doubt the likelihood of subsequent tightening. The Australian Dollar traded in response to the monetary decision.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of Australia executed a benchmark rate increase. Foreign exchange desks priced the immediate rate trajectory while discounting subsequent policy tightening. Commerzbank strategists highlighted that market implied pricing limits additional hikes. The Australian Dollar absorbed the policy adjustment.
